notes: This contract pins Umbra's bounded implementation of the official 2025 C++ RTI/auth/HLAplainTextPassword.h value class, the reference HLAauthorizer/AuthorizerFactory/HLAauthorizerFactoryFactory behavior, the separate static library-level AuthorizerFactoryFactory forwarding boundary, and the current embedded profile's disabled-authorization Connect behavior. IEEE 1516.1-2025 §12.6 requires the HLAplainTextPassword constructor to set its predefined type and encode its supplied text as HLAunicodeString; Umbra therefore delegates both encoding and validation to the completed standard HLAunicodeString helper rather than defining a password byte format. The private ReferenceAuthorizerConfiguration seam permits deterministic unit tests of the reference global-password behavior, but no public configuration selects it and the public factory is intentionally unconfigured until a secure RID-backed configuration/lifecycle exists. The runtime therefore still has no configured authorization service: a no-credentials Connect overload remains available, an explicit empty HLAnoCredentials envelope is accepted as the standard no-credentials form, and another supplied Credentials envelope is rejected as Unauthorized rather than silently treated as authenticated. The static umbra_authorizer target preserves the C++ forwarding boundary only; it does not claim completion of the SISO library-nomenclature/dynamic-link, custom-authorizer, secure configuration, Connect/Create/Destroy/Join lifecycle, adapter, catalog/JUnit/package, interoperability, security-review, or conformance work. The direct page-357 candidates retain exported Annex/§12.8 provenance even though the reconstructed source places the relevant text in §§12.5-12.6; RL-056 records that source-export drift. RL-057 records that the reconstructed authorization-library prose says getAuthorizationFactory while the official C++ headers declare getAuthorizerFactory, the spelling used by Umbra.
